text.p: - It is inappropriate for Russia to seek union with a pro-Soviet politician who has dared to back Stalin and Hitler in public, says a front-page letter signed by a group of Russian intellectuals.
- Output at the Voronezh Mechanical Plant (southern Russia) grew by 12.5 percent last year after its administration turned its back on ideology, the paper says on its front page.
- The former chief of Russia's Antimonopoly Committee Leonid Bochin has been appointed to the Moscow government to step up the fight against ecological problems in the capital.
- Russia received 59 per cent of targeted budget revenues in the first three months of this year.
- Integration is like cheese, free only when it's in a mouse trap, says the paper in connection with public discussion of the union with Belarus.
- International Monetary Fund (IMF) managing director Michel Camdessus unpleasantly surprised Russia's new cabinet on Tuesday by toughening conditions for disbursing the fund's delayed loan.
- The Union Treaty with Belarus is being strongly critisised for ignoring Russia's economic interests.
- Ukranian President Leonid Kuchma opposes any union on CIS territory like that which Russia is planning with Belarus.
- President Boris Yeltsin has regained the top position in a list of Russia's hundred leading politicians, according to an independent survey.
- Russians will gain a lot from union with Belarus - a country with a stable economy, regular wages and pension payments and home-produced food for its population.
- NATO was supposed to be frightened by the Union Treaty with Belarus but Russians seem to have been more scared so far.
- The wind in Moscow was so strong on Tuesday that it blew pieces of a kiosk over a fence and onto the rails of an open section of the underground railway. Fortunately noone was hurt.
